A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ToolVQA dataset and ToolEngine pipeline. Text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material are readable. v1 ends after its references; v2 retains the main paper and adds supplementary Sections 6–11.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, data-construction and training ablations, few-shot experiments, and error analysis in Tables 3–7 and Figure 7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports the user tool-use frequency distribution in Figure 8.

M1.justification: The DFS pipeline, LCS-based example selection and fine-tuning objective are unchanged. The supplement documents implementation choices, including initial ImageCaption/OCR use, LoRA and controller prompts; it does not establish a version-to-version change in the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use ToolVQA and the same five OOD benchmarks: TextVQA, TallyQA, InfoSeek, GTA and TEMPLAMA. Supplementary participant descriptions and example galleries document existing data collection and coverage rather than new populations or evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main benchmark, OOD, few-shot and ablation tables. Newly cited software and tool implementations in the supplement are not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The existing splits, evaluation modes, model settings and metrics are retained. Section 9 newly specifies the 1,622 text-answer end-to-end examples, OOD subsampling and TextVQA OCR-token exclusion, but presents these as details of existing experiments rather than revised protocols.

E4.justification: Figure 8 adds a descriptive analysis of real users' tool frequencies, supporting toolset selection and allowing comparison with the dataset frequencies in Figure 5. Existing ablations and error analysis are unchanged; Figures 9–10 provide illustrative trajectories rather than new robustness experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. Additional annotation and sampling details do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical values and rankings. New descriptive results include Figure 8's user frequencies, such as Search at 30.8% and Caption at 23.6%, and Section 9.2's statement that tool-use VQA takes approximately 4–6 times as long as conventional VQA.

T1.justification: The task formulation, training loss and LCS-based retrieval expression are unchanged. Algorithm 1 supplies standard dynamic-programming pseudocode for the already specified LCS operation, without adding a theorem, proof or substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same dataset, pipeline and generalization claims. The claim of outperforming GPT-3.5-Turbo on all five OOD benchmarks also remains, despite both versions' Table 5 reporting lower TEMPLAMA accuracy: 21.43 versus 33.67.

C2.justification: The supplement expands the rationale for general-purpose tools and LCS matching, explains the computational motivation for initial caption/OCR use, and states evaluation boundaries involving image answers and externally supplied OCR tokens. Main-text interpretations of model bottlenecks and errors remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies substantial previously absent reproduction information: tool backends and interfaces in Table 8, construction of 34 examples from 150 user scenarios, matching pseudocode, prompt templates, LoRA training settings and hardware, and detailed evaluation and answer-matching procedures. These are disclosures about the existing work; the code-access URL is unchanged.

R1.justification: All 50 original references are retained, with 11 additions supporting supplementary implementation and evaluation details, including LoRA, XTuner, OpenCompass, OCRBench and Tree of Thoughts. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain essentially unchanged apart from citation renumbering and text reflow. v2 adds an organized supplement with an overview, procedural explanations and prompt transcripts, extending the supporting structure without extensively rewriting the paper.

P2.justification: The supplement substantially expands visual documentation through Table 8, Algorithm 1, the user-frequency chart and two organized galleries showing trajectories and answer annotations. Figure 9 expands some examples already illustrated in Figure 3. Existing main-paper figures and tables retain their presentation.

improvement.justification: The supplement addresses important reproducibility omissions in v1 by specifying tool implementations, prompts, data-construction procedures, training settings and evaluation subsets. This substantially improves readers' ability to inspect and reproduce the central contribution without changing benchmark performance. There are flaws: Figure 9 gives '26' for an apple-producing-area question whose tool output says 'Washington', and the existing OOD overclaim remains uncorrected. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial gain in methodological transparency.
